# ROUND-4 fixture (HIGH): the negative twin of makefile-trust-positive.
#
# makefile-trust-positive proves compute_makefile_trust says TRUE for a real
# recipe (so the native step is correctly skipped). Nothing proved it says
# FALSE for a recipe that only LOOKS real - and it didn't: Make's `-`
# (ignore-error) prefix was never handled, so a `-true` recipe was classified
# non-trivial, earned full trust, and SKIPPED the native step. That is the
# original H2 false-green failure class, reached through `-` instead of the
# already-handled `@`.
#
# HOW THIS BITES: the root Makefile's `lint:` target has a recipe of
# `-true`, and its comment names THIS directory - so the directory-mention
# half of compute_makefile_trust is satisfied, and the ONLY thing standing
# between this fixture and trust=true is is_trivial_makefile_recipe
# recognising the `-` prefix. If it stops recognising it, `ruff check .` is
# skipped for this job, unused_import.py's deliberate F401 is never seen, and
# the job goes GREEN - which its assert job (expecting failure, and grepping
# this job's real log for ruff's own F401 output) then reports as the
# regression it is.
#
# Root-directory coverage (directory == '.') is deliberately NOT here: it
# would need a real Python/Node manifest at this repo's own root, which
# self-test.yml's root-makefile-and-semgrep comment already explains is a
# trade-off not worth making. scripts/test-makefile-trust.sh covers that half
# directly, against the same helper functions extracted from the workflow.
#
# No runtime dependencies - this file exists only so has_python evaluates
# true for this directory, which is what makes the native `ruff check .` step
# eligible to run at all.
